tagline: Mist over Khao Kho, chilly nights on Phu Tab Berk, and the sweet tamarind the province is known for
introHtml: Phetchabun is where people from Bangkok and the central plains like to drive up for cool weather as the rainy season turns to winter. The province sits in a valley ringed by mountains, with Khao Kho and Phu Tab Berk where an early start often gets you a sea of mist. Up on Phu Tab Berk there are cabbage fields stepping down the slopes and Hmong villages to stop at. If you're into history, the ancient town of Si Thep was just listed as a World Heritage Site. The food to take home is the sweet tamarind and sweet corn grown all over the province. One trip to Phetchabun gives you mountains, temples, and a car full of things to bring back.
bestTime: November–January is coldest, with mist rolling in often — this is when Khao Kho and Phu Tab Berk are busiest

highlights.name: Khao Kho
highlights.blurb: A cool-weather mountain full of resorts and mist viewpoints. You can spend all day driving around looking at tea fields, flower farms, and stays with mountain views

highlights.name: Phu Tab Berk
highlights.blurb: The highest point in the province, with cabbage fields stepping down the slopes as its signature view. Start early for the sea of mist and bitterly cold air in winter

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaeo
highlights.blurb: A temple on Khao Kho with its pagoda covered in brightly colored tiles and ceramic bowls. It sits on a rise looking out over wide mountain views

highlights.name: Si Thep Ancient Town
highlights.blurb: A Dvaravati-era ancient town listed as a World Heritage Site, with the Khao Klang Nok monument and the Si Thep prang to walk around

highlights.name: Phetchabun sweet tamarind
highlights.blurb: The province's signature, grown everywhere. In winter the markets fill with sweet tamarind — buy it to take home as whole pods or processed snacks

highlights.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla
highlights.blurb: A national park on the Phetchabun–Phitsanulok border, with a cracked-rock field, Pha Chu Thong cliff, and Communist-era history to explore on foot

foodScene.name: Sweet tamarind and tamarind snacks
foodScene.note: The province's top souvenir, sold all along the road as fresh pods, tamarind tossed with sugar, tamarind candy, and tangy spiced tamarind

foodScene.name: Sweet corn
foodScene.note: Grown all over Phetchabun and boiled fresh at roadside stalls on the way up Khao Kho — sweet and juicy, easy to grab and eat on the drive

foodScene.name: Hmong food on Phu Tab Berk
foodScene.note: Restaurants up on Phu Tab Berk keep it simple — black chicken in Chinese herbal soup, fresh vegetables from the farm, and hot rice porridge to fight the cold

foodScene.name: Khao Kho grilled pork
foodScene.note: Marinated pork grilled over charcoal at roadside stalls on Khao Kho, eaten with warm sticky rice — a go-to bite on a mountain trip

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laab are easy to find around town, since Phetchabun has a large Isan community. Bold and satisfying

foodScene.name: Noodles and rice-and-curry in town
foodScene.note: Downtown Phetchabun has noodle shops and rice-and-curry stalls at local prices for an easy meal before heading up the mountain

foodScene.name: Mountain-view cafes on Khao Kho
foodScene.note: Khao Kho has plenty of cafes where you can sip coffee looking out at the mountains and the mist — a popular place to take a break

foodScene.name: Mookata (Thai BBQ hotpot)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner in town and at mountain stays. Eaten hot, it's just right for the cold weather

attractions.name: Khao Kho
attractions.blurb: A cool-weather mountain with mist viewpoints, tea fields, flower farms, and stays with mountain views — a full day of driving around

attractions.name: Phu Tab Berk
attractions.blurb: The highest point in the province. See cabbage fields stepping down the slopes and the morning sea of mist, with bitterly cold air in winter

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaeo
attractions.blurb: A temple on Khao Kho, its pagoda covered in brightly colored tiles and ceramic bowls, with wide mountain views all around

attractions.name: Si Thep Ancient Town
attractions.blurb: A Dvaravati-era ancient town and World Heritage Site — walk around Khao Klang Nok, the Si Thep prang, and the old city moat

attractions.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla
attractions.blurb: A national park on the border with Phitsanulok, with a cracked-rock field, Pha Chu Thong cliff, and traces of history to explore on foot

attractions.name: Mueang Rat–Pho Khun Pha Mueang Memorial
attractions.blurb: A memorial to the province's history — a stop to pay respects and learn about the old town on the way up the mountain

attractions.name: Khao Kho Royal Residence–Sacrifice Memorial
attractions.blurb: A viewpoint on Khao Kho with a memorial from the years of fighting, looking out over ranges of mountains as far as you can see

attractions.name: B.N. Farm and Khao Kho flower fields
attractions.blurb: A flower farm and mountain-view photo spot on Khao Kho — in winter the fields are full of blooms to wander through
